\title{The Goncharov Lie coalgebra of a field}
\author{Alexander Kupers \and Daniil Rudenko \and Ismael Sierra}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\noindent\textbf{Source:} \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23863}{arXiv:2606.23863} \quad \textbf{Field:} math.KT\\

\section*{TL;DR}
This paper introduces the Goncharov Lie coalgebra G(F) of a field F as the E\ensuremath{\infty}-homology of BGL(F)\_Q along the critical line, presents it by generators (correlators) and four families of relations (homogeneity, cyclic symmetry, shuffle, decomposition), computes the Lie cobracket, constructs motivic and Hodge realisations, and proves a weight-3 K-theory theorem (Theorem 1) via the Rognes rank spectral sequence. The novelty specialist rates the work 0.82/significant, and the related-work survey confirms the paper makes clear advances beyond GKRW20 and CharltonRadchenkoRudenko by providing the explicit presentation and cobracket and using them to derive new K-theory results. The technical-correctness specialist (confidence 0.55, mostly\_sound) finds no outright errors but flags two unsupported claims at major severity --- computer-assisted scripts for Section 7.3.3 and missing proof-as-code artifacts for the headline theorems --- and several partially-supported claims (C2, C3, C5, C6, C11) where key intermediate steps are deferred or only asserted. The reproducibility specialist (score 0.22) escalates one concern to critical: no proof-as-code artifact accompanies the isomorphism K\_4\^{}(3)(F)\_Q ≅ H\^{}2(G(F))\_3. The paper's field (math.KT / math.AT) is code-amenable; the Recommendation Gate therefore defaults to major\_revision, since reproducibility flagged a critical missing artifact and technical\_correctness flagged two major unsupported proof-as-code claims. The citation audit (confidence 0.62) covers only 32 of 122 entries but notes a duplicate preprint/published pair (CMRR/CMRR24) and one web-archive-only citation. Specialists do not disagree on the paper's mathematical significance; the split is entirely between the strength of the mathematics and the absence of companion artifacts for the computer-assisted and mechanizable portions.

\textbf{Recommendation:} Major revision \quad \textbf{Confidence:} 72\%\\

\section*{Strengths}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item The construction of G(F) as E\ensuremath{\infty}-homology of BGL(F)\_Q is conceptually original and establishes a long-sought bridge between stable homological algebra of GL and the analytic theory of multiple polylogarithms.
  \item The explicit presentation of G(F) by correlator generators subject to homogeneity, cyclic symmetry, shuffle, and decomposition relations provides a finite, computable, generator-and-relations description that previous homotopy-theoretic definitions lacked.
  \item Theorem 1 proves K\_4\^{}(3)(F)\_Q ≅ H\^{}2(G(F))\_3 and derives an exact sequence for K\_5\^{}(3)(F)\_Q via the Rognes RSS, yielding a new proof of and extension to the Bolbachan--Goncharov conjecture at weight 3, with a simultaneous equivalence to Beilinson--Soulé vanishing as a sanity check.
  \item The low-weight identifications G\_1(F) ≅ F\^{}\ensuremath{\times}\_Q, G\_2(F) ≅ B\_2(F)\_Q, G\_3(F) ≅ B\_3(F)\_Q confirm the framework recovers the classical results of Milnor, Matsumoto, Bloch, and Suslin, grounding the abstract construction in well-tested territory.
  \item Construction of both motivic and Hodge realisation functors R\^{}MTM and R\^{}Hod, mapping comodule categories of G(F) to MTM\_Q(F) and mixed Hodge-Tate structures, provides a concrete path toward the full isomorphism G(F) ≅ L\^{}MTM(F) claimed for the sequel.
  \item The paper situates its construction carefully among the competing candidates (Bloch-Kriz 1-minimal model, Aomoto Hopf algebra, formal polylogarithm coalgebra), and the comparison maps r\^{}f, r\^{}MTM, r\^{}Hod are all made explicit.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Weaknesses}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item Computer-assisted computations verifying trilogarithm functional equations in Section 7.3.3 are acknowledged in the acknowledgments (crediting Steven Charlton) but no script, data file, or reproducible artifact is provided, leaving a major proof step unverifiable.
  \item No proof-as-code artifact --- Lean, Coq, or executable symbolic computation --- accompanies the presentation theorem, cobracket theorem, or headline K-theory isomorphism, despite the combinatorial portions (decomposition relation index set, shuffle closure, n=3 cobracket expansion) being mechanizable in a proof assistant.
  \item The spectral-sequence collapse-in-range argument underlying Theorem 1 (claims C5, C6, C11) does not state explicitly which higher Rognes RSS differentials vanish in the weight-3 region; the derivation currently relies on Figures 5--6 without a precise reference to the section supplying the vanishing proof.
  \item The projectivity of the formal-correlator module FC(V) over GL(V) and the exactness of the decomposition resolution eqn:dec-resolution beyond the first two terms are stated but not proved in the bounded text (claim C2), leaving the completeness of the presentation theorem on an unstated assumption.
  \item The cobracket construction via the zigzag H/H\^{}2 \ensuremath{\leftarrow} H/H\^{}3 \ensuremath{\to} H/H\^{}2 \ensuremath{\otimes} H/H\^{}2 requires a choice of lift, and the paper explicitly flags this subtlety (claim C3) but does not resolve it in the introduction or provide a low-weight verification (e.g., n=2 coJacobi check).
  \item Bibliography entries CMRR and CMRR24 are duplicate records for the same Charlton--Matveiakin--Radchenko--Rudenko paper (preprint and published version), and AlekseevTorossianNote cites an unpublished note available only via a Wayback Machine archive, raising long-term accessibility concerns.
  \item The identification G\_3(F) ≅ B\_3(F)\_Q, which is the hinge connecting Theorem polyl-identification to Theorem 1, is stated without surfacing the step showing that the G\_3-defining relations coincide with Goncharov's B\_3-relations (claim C4).
\end{itemize}

\section*{Open Questions}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
  \item Which higher differentials of the Rognes rank spectral sequence are explicitly shown to vanish in the weight-3 bidegree range used by Theorem 1, and in which section of the paper is this proved?
  \item Can the computer-assisted computations verifying the trilogarithm functional equations of Section 7.3.3 be made available as reproducible scripts (e.g., a SageMath or Python file computing the relevant linear-algebra checks over Q)?
  \item What is the precise lift chosen in the zigzag construction of the Lie cobracket (Section 5.3.1), and how is independence of that choice established --- is there a direct co-Jacobi verification at low weight?
  \item Where in the text is the step proved that the relations defining G\_3(F) via the decomposition resolution reduce exactly to Goncharov's B\_3(F)-relations, rather than a potentially larger quotient?
  \item Given that Bolbachan [Bol24] proves K\_4\^{}(3)(F)\_Q ≅ B\_3(F)\_Q by a different method, can the authors clarify at what level the two proofs diverge, and whether the Rognes-RSS approach yields additional structural information (e.g., the edge map or the exact sequence for K\_5\^{}(3)) that Bol24's argument does not?
  \item The formal-to-motivic map L\^{}f(F) \ensuremath{\to} L\^{}MTM(F) (used to define r\^{}MTM) is asserted to be well-defined by sending formal correlators to Goncharov's motivic correlators: which specific relations of L\^{}f are mapped to known identities among Cor\^{}MTM in [Gon19], and where is this verified?
\end{itemize}

This paper defines G(F) as the critical-line E\ensuremath{\infty}-homology, provides a complete presentation via correlators with explicit generators and four families of relations, derives an explicit cobracket formula, and deploys the resulting structure to prove new K-th…",\\

      "text": "CharltonRadchenkoRudenko gave a presentation of St\^{}\ensuremath{\infty}\_n via Steinberg correlators and computed the cobracket on H\_1(GL\_n; St\^{}\ensuremath{\infty}\_n).       "verifier\_status": "pass"\\

      "id": "claim\_46",\\
      "role": "novelty",\\
      "text": "Goncharov defined B\_3(F) and the weight 3 polylogarithmic complex \ensuremath{\Gamma}\_3(F) and conjectured that its homology groups compute K\_5\^{}(3), K\_4\^{}(3), and K\^{}M\_3(F). \$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-homology of general linear groups \{\#sec:intro-einfty\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe start by recalling the approach to studying the homology of general\textbackslash{}nlinear groups introduced by Galatius, Kupers, and Randal-Williams\textbackslash{}n[@GKRW18; @GKRW19; @GKRW20] and how it leads to the Goncharov Lie\textbackslash{}ncoalgebra. This takes place in a homotopy-theoretic context, so we work\textbackslash{}nin \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-categories or, if the reader prefers, suitable model\textbackslash{}ncategories.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n\#\#\#\# The \$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-algebra \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThe block sum of matrices induces a product on chains\textbackslash{}n\$\$C\_*(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{GL\}\}\_n(F);\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\})\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes C\_*(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{GL\}\}\_m(F);\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow C\_*(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{GL\}\}\_\{n+m\}(F);\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\})\$\$\textbackslash{}nwhich is associative and commutative up to chain homotopy. It is\textbackslash{}nconvenient to keep track of the dimension (or *rank*) \$n\$ by defining a\textbackslash{}nfunctor \$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{align*\}\textbackslash{}n\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}colon \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{N\}\} \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{D\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}nn \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longmapsto C\_*(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{BGL\}\}\_n(F);\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}),\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{align*\}\$\$ where \$\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{D\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\}\$ is the derived\textbackslash{}ncategory of \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$ obtained by inverting the quasi-isomorphisms\textbackslash{}nin the category of rational chain complexes. That the above product\textbackslash{}nadmits coherent associativity or commutativity chain homotopies means\textbackslash{}nthat this functor lifts to a nonunital \$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-algebra\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Alg\}\}\_\{E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\^{}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{nu\}\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Fun\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{N\}\},\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{D\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\}))\$,\textbackslash{}nwhere \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Fun\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{N\}\},\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{D\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\})\$ is\textbackslash{}nendowed with the Day convolution symmetric monoidal structure.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThere is a well-developed theory of derived indecomposables of nonunital\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-algebras such as \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$,\textbackslash{}ne.g. [@GKRW18]. Informally this recovers its generators and relations,\textbackslash{}nas homotopy-theoretically there is no distinction between these. More\textbackslash{}nprecisely, the functor making an object into a nonunital\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-algebra with trivial multiplication has a left adjoint\textbackslash{}n\$\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cot\}\}\_\{E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\^{}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{nu\}\}\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}colon \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Alg\}\}\_\{E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\^{}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{nu\}\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Fun\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{N\}\},\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{D\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\})) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Fun\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{N\}\},\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{D\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\})\$\$\textbackslash{}nknown as the *cotangent complex* or *\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-indecomposables*; we\textbackslash{}nwill use the latter terminology. In our rational setting, it may be\textbackslash{}ncomputed by strictifying to a commutative dg-algebra and taking Harrison\textbackslash{}nhomology; for example, for a minimal commutative dg-algebra this yields\textbackslash{}nits indecomposables in an underived sense, which are canonically\textbackslash{}nisomorphic to its generators.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThe *\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-homology groups* of \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$ are\textbackslash{}nthen defined as\textbackslash{}n\$\$H\^{}\{E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\}\_\{n,d\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneq H\_d(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cot\}\}\_\{E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\^{}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{nu\}\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\})(n))\$\$\textbackslash{}nand one of the main results of [@GKRW20] is a determination of some of\textbackslash{}nthese groups, see [1](\#fig:gltable1)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"fig:gltable1\textbackslash{}"\}: in particular, they vanish for \$d \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}leq 2n-2\$\textbackslash{}nwith the exception of \$(n,d) = (1,0)\$. The Goncharov Lie coalgebra is\textbackslash{}ndefined as those entries on the critical line above where this vanishing\textbackslash{}nresult applies:\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}(F) = \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}bigoplus\_\{n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}geq 1\} H\_\{n,2n-1\}\^{}\{E\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\}\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}).\$\$\textbackslash{}nIts name is justified by Koszul duality between the nonunital\textbackslash{}ncommutative operad and the suspended Lie cooperad, which implies that\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-indecomposables admit the structure of a shifted Lie\textbackslash{}ncoalgebra: for a minimal commutative dg-algebra this is the quadratic\textbackslash{}npart of the differential on generators. This endows the\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-homology groups\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{H\^{}\{E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\}\_\{n,d\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\})\}\$ with a\textbackslash{}ncobracket of degree \$-1\$, restricting to a Lie coalgebra structure on\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}(F)\$; the gradings work out to make so that Lie cobracket\textbackslash{}ndoes not involve additional Koszul signs. It is a construction for\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-algebras with a slope 2 vanishing line that is analogous to\textbackslash{}nthe \textbackslash{}"stability Hopf algebra\textbackslash{}" of [@RWchromatic] for \$E\_2\$-algebras with a\textbackslash{}nslope 1 vanishing line, and encodes the attaching maps for\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-cells in the sense of [@GKRW18].\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n<figure id=\textbackslash{}"fig:gltable1\textbackslash{}" data-latex-placement=\textbackslash{}"h\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n<figcaption>The <span class=\textbackslash{}"math inline\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}(E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{})</span>-homology\textbackslash{}nof <span class=\textbackslash{}"math inline\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbf\{BGL\}\}(F)\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{})</span>,\textbackslash{}nwhich vanishes for <span class=\textbackslash{}"math inline\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}(d \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}leq 2n-2\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{})</span> as\textbackslash{}nlong as <span class=\textbackslash{}"math inline\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}(n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}geq 2\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{})</span>. We will first recall the Steinberg modules and their\textbackslash{}ndouble and infinite variants, giving a particularly nice generating set\textbackslash{}nfor the latter, and explain how these are related to the\textbackslash{}n\$E\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-homology groups discussed in the previous subsection.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n\#\#\#\# Steinberg modules, double Steinberg modules, and infinite Steinberg modules\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThe *Tits building* \$T(F\^{}n)\$ is defined as the geometric realisation of\textbackslash{}nthe nerve of the poset of proper nonzero subspaces of \$F\^{}n\$. By the\textbackslash{}nSolomon--Tits theorem it is equivalent to a wedge of \$(n-2)\$-spheres,\textbackslash{}nand its top reduced rational homology is a \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{GL\}\}\_n(F)\$-module\textbackslash{}nknown as the *Steinberg module*\textbackslash{}n\$\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{St\}\}\_n(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneq \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}widetilde\{H\}\_\{n-2\}(T(F\^{}n);\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}).\$\$\textbackslash{}nThis has a well-known presentation with generators given by apartment\textbackslash{}nclasses \$[v\_1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathinner\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\},v\_n]\$\textbackslash{}nindexed by ordered bases\textbackslash{}n\$v\_1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathinner\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\},v\_n\$; we suggest\textbackslash{}nrepresenting these by simplices in projective space\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{P\}\}\^{}\{n-1\}(F)\$ as on the left of\textbackslash{}n[2](\#fig:generators-st-sth)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"fig:generators-st-sth\textbackslash{}"\}.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n<figure id=\textbackslash{}"fig:generators-st-sth\textbackslash{}" data-latex-placement=\textbackslash{}"h\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n<figcaption>A generator of <span\textbackslash{}nclass=\textbackslash{}"math inline\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{St\}\}\_3(F)\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{})</span> (on the left) and a\textbackslash{}ngenerator of <span class=\textbackslash{}"math inline\textbackslash{}">\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{St\}\}\^{}\{2\}\_3(F)\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{})</span>\textbackslash{}n(on the right).</figcaption>\textbackslash{}n</figure>\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nTo explain further structure, we organise all Steinberg modules into a\textbackslash{}nsingle object. Let \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Vect\}\}\_F\$ denote the groupoid of\textbackslash{}nfinite-dimensional vector spaces over \$F\$ and linear isomorphisms, then\textbackslash{}nwe can think of the Steinberg modules as a functor (with\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{St\}\}(V)\$ in degree \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}dim(V)\$) \$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{align*\}\textbackslash{}n\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{S\}\}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{t\}\}\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}colon \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Vect\}\}\_F \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{GrMod\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}nV \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longmapsto \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{St\}\}(V).\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{align*\}\$\$ The category \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Vect\}\}\_F\$ admits not only a\textbackslash{}nsymmetric monoidal structure given by direct sum but also a promonoidal\textbackslash{}nstructure given by \textbackslash{}"flag sum\textbackslash{}", which assemble to a produoidal category.\textbackslash{}nBy Day convolution, these induce on functors\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Vect\}\}\_F \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{GrMod\}\}\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$ a symmetric\textbackslash{}nmonoidal structure whose tensor product \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}boxplus\$ we call the *Levi\textbackslash{}ntensor product* and a monoidal structure whose tensor product\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}boxbackslash\$ we call the *parabolic tensor product*, which assemble\textbackslash{}nto a duoidal category. decomposition relation is not entirely new: from the viewpoint of\textbackslash{}niterated integrals, it is a natural instance of the classical\textbackslash{}nchange-of-variable formalism for iterated integrals. In some sense, it\textbackslash{}nis the simplest general functional equation for multiple\textbackslash{}npolylogarithms/iterated integrals/correlators one can write down. To\textbackslash{}nexplain the idea behind it, we work with iterated integrals as\textbackslash{}nmultivalued functions, defined by\textbackslash{}n\$\$I\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma(a\_0;a\_1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathinner\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\},a\_n;a\_\{n+1\})\textbackslash{}n=\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}int\_\{0\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}le t\_1\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}le \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cdots \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}le t\_n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}le 1\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}frac\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma'(t\_1)\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{},dt\_1\}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma(t\_1)-a\_1\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cdots\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}frac\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma'(t\_n)\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{},dt\_n\}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma(t\_n)-a\_n\}\$\$ for a path\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}colon [0,1]\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbb C\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}setminus\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\{a\_1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldots,a\_n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\}\$ with start\textbackslash{}npoint \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma(0)=a\_0\$, end point \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}gamma(1)=a\_\{n+1\}\$. It is well-known,\textbackslash{}ne.g. [@Gon01 Theorem 2.1], that the iterated integral\textbackslash{}n\$\$I(f\_0(t);f\_1(t),\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathinner\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\},f\_n(t);f\_\{n+1\}(t)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}qquad \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{for rational functions \$f\_i(t)\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\}(t)\$\}\$\$\textbackslash{}ncan be rewritten, after choosing branches and possibly enlarging the set\textbackslash{}nof singularities, as a linear combination of hyperlogarithms in the\textbackslash{}nvariable \$t\$, i.e. of iterated integrals of the form\textbackslash{}n\$\$I(a\_0;a\_1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathinner\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\},a\_n;t) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}qquad \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{for constants \$a\_0, \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldots,a\_\{n\}\$.\}\$\$\textbackslash{}nThis idea has appeared in the literature before, for instance, in the\textbackslash{}nwork of Wojtkowiak [@Wojtkowiak]. The same heuristic applies to\textbackslash{}nanalytic, Hodge, motivic, or formal iterated integrals and correlators.\textbackslash{}nIn \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}\}(F)\$, the resulting expansion for\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Cor\}\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}(x\_0+y\_0t,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathinner\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mkern-2mu\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldotp\},x\_n+y\_nt)\$\$\textbackslash{}nis precisely the decomposition relation upon evaluation at \$t=0,1\$. Its\textbackslash{}nlinear dual can be identified with the quotient of the free\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Z\}\}[\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{S\}\}\_n]\$-module on a single generator by\textbackslash{}n\$(i,n-i)\$-shuffles for \$1 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}leq i \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}leq n-1\$ [@Whitehouse Theorem 2.6].\textbackslash{}n(Over a field \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{k\}\}\$ of characteristic zero, there is a\textbackslash{}nnoncanonical isomorphism \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\_n\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}vee\$\textbackslash{}nbut this is not the case over the integers, and we find it illuminating\textbackslash{}nto distinguish them.)\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nBy construction, we may identify \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\_n\$ with the space of\textbackslash{}n\$n\$-ary operations of the operad \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\$. Since the operad\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\$ extends to a cyclic operad \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\}\$\textbackslash{}n[@GetzlerKapranov 3.9(c)], \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\_n\$ must be the restriction of\textbackslash{}na \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Z\}\}[\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{S\}\}\_\{n+1\}]\$-module \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\}\_n\$ and\textbackslash{}ndually \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}vee\_n\$ must be the restriction of a\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Z\}\}[\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{S\}\}\_\{n+1\}]\$-module \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\}\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}vee\_n\$.\textbackslash{}nThe former can be described as\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Z\}\}[\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{S\}\}\_\{n+1\}]\$-module of trivalent trees with a\textbackslash{}ncyclic order at each vertex whose leaves are in bijection with the set\textbackslash{}n\$[n] = \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\{0,1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ldots,n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\}\$, modulo AS and IHX relations; we call these\textbackslash{}n*cyclic Lie trees*. The latter was described by Whitehouse:\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\}\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}vee\_n\$ is the quotient of the free\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Z\}\}[\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{S\}\}\_\{n+1\}]\$-module on a single generator by\textbackslash{}n\$(i,n-i)\$-shuffles for \$1 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}leq i \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}leq n-1\$ and cyclic symmetry\textbackslash{}n[@Whitehouse p. 317, 319].\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n\#\#\#\# Lie variant \{\#sec:trees-lie\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThere is a closely related Lie variant of the associative construction\textbackslash{}nin [3.2.1](\#sec:trees-as)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"sec:trees-as\textbackslash{}"\}, and in explaining it we mostly follow\textbackslash{}n[@AlekseevTorossian]. We again fix a finite set \$S\$ and consider the\textbackslash{}nfree Lie algebra on the vector space\textbackslash{}n\$V\_S = \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\{X\_s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mid s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\}\$ of symbols \$X\_s\$ for \$s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\$:\textbackslash{}n\$\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneq \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{free\}\}\_\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\}(V\_S).\$\$\textbackslash{}nThis admits a description in terms of Lie trees: let\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{rtree\}\}\_S\$ be the vector space spanned by isomorphism\textbackslash{}nclasses of rooted finite trivalent trees with a cyclic order at each\textbackslash{}nvertex whose leaves are labelled by elements from the set of symbols\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\{X\_s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mid s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\}\$, modulo the AS and IHX relations. Additively, this space is given by first\textbackslash{}nrecalling that the Lie operad \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Lie\}\}\$ extends to a cyclic\textbackslash{}noperad \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\}\$ and then taking\textbackslash{}n\$\$|\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S| \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneq \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}bigoplus\_\{n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}geq 1\} \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\}\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes\_\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{S\}\}\_\{n+1\}\} V\_S\^{}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes (n+1)\}.\$\$\textbackslash{}nThat is, there is an isomorphism \$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{align*\}\textbackslash{}n |\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S|/\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}textstyle \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}prod\_\{s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\} |\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_s|\} \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{sder\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}n    |a| \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longmapsto (a\_s)\_\{s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\}.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{align*\}\$\$ This admits a description in terms of cyclic Lie trees:\textbackslash{}nlet \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{tree\}\}\_S\$ be the vector space spanned by isomorphism\textbackslash{}nclasses of finite trivalent trees with a cyclic order at each vertex\textbackslash{}nwhose leaves are labelled by elements from \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\{X\_s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mid s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\}\$,\textbackslash{}nmodulo the AS and IHX relations. Equivalence classes of cyclic Lie trees\textbackslash{}ncorrespond to cyclic Lie words in the alphabet \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\{X\_s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mid s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\}\$,\textbackslash{}nin the sense that there is an isomorphism of vector spaces\textbackslash{}n\$\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{tree\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow|\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S|.\$\$\textbackslash{}nThere is an isomorphism \$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{align*\}\textbackslash{}n\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{tree\}\}\_S/\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}textstyle \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}prod\_\{s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\} \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{tree\}\}\_s\} \& \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{sder\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longmapsto (a\_s)\_\{s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{align*\}\$\$ given on a tree \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\$ by letting \$a\_s\$ be given by a\textbackslash{}nsum over all leaves of \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\$ with label \$s\$, of the Lie tree obtained\textbackslash{}nby interpreting that leaf as a root [@AlekseevTorossian Section 2.2.1]\textbackslash{}n(see also [@Felder Appendix A]). Under this isomorphism, the Lie bracket\textbackslash{}non \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{sder\}\}\_S\$ is given as follows: for two cyclic Lie trees\textbackslash{}n\$T\_1,T\_2\$, the bracket \$[T\_1,T\_2]\$ is given by the sum over all\textbackslash{}n\$s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\$, all leaves of \$T\_1\$ labelled by \$X\_s\$, and all leaves of\textbackslash{}n\$T\_2\$ labelled by \$X\_s\$, of \$T\_1\$ and \$T\_2\$ joined at these leaves to a\textbackslash{}ntrivalent vertex with positive orientation and remaining leaf labelled\textbackslash{}nby \$X\_s\$. Similarly, the action of \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{sder\}\}\_S\$ on\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S\$ is given as follows: for a cyclic Lie tree \$T\$ and\textbackslash{}na rooted Lie tree \$R\$, \$D\_T(R)\$ is given by the sum over \$s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in S\$, all\textbackslash{}nleaves of \$T\$ labelled by \$X\_s\$, and all leaves of \$R\$ labelled by\textbackslash{}n\$X\_s\$, of those leaves joined into a single edge.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n\#\#\#\# Comparison of the associative and Lie variant \{\#sec:trees-comp\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nAs the similarity of the descriptions of the associative and Lie\textbackslash{}nvariants suggests, there are inclusions\textbackslash{}n\$\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathsf\{as\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}qquad \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{and\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}qquad \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{sder\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathsf\{sder\}\}\_S\$\$\textbackslash{}ngiven by including a free Lie algebra into its universal enveloping\textbackslash{}nalgebra and uniquely extending a special derivation of a free Lie\textbackslash{}nalgebra to the one of its universal enveloping algebra. It is clear from\textbackslash{}nthe constructions that these maps are compatible with the Lie brackets\textbackslash{}non the free algebras and special derivations, and the actions of special\textbackslash{}nderivations on the corresponding free algebras [@AKKN p. 7].\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n\#\#\#\# Relationship to universal traces\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThe above discussion is related to universal invariant bilinear forms,\textbackslash{}ndue to Drinfeld [@Drinfeld p. 856]: for a Lie algebra \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{g\}\}\$\textbackslash{}ndefine a vector space\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{F\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{g\}\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneqq \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}frac\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{g\}\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{g\}\}\}\{[X,Y] \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes Z - X \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes [Y,Z] \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{ and \} X\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes Y-Y \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes X\}.\$\$\textbackslash{}nIn [@AlekseevTorossianNote Section 2.2] it is proven that there is an\textbackslash{}nisomorphism of vector spaces\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{F\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{tree\}\}\_S\$\$\textbackslash{}ngiven on a pair \$X \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes Y\$ of Lie words in the \$X\_s\$ by interpreting\textbackslash{}nthem as rooted trees and connecting their roots. In [@Drinfeld p. 857],\textbackslash{}nDrinfeld described the composite homomorphism\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{F\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{lie\}\}\_S) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{tree\}\}\_S \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{sder\}\}\_S\$\$\textbackslash{}nwhich is a surjection of Lie algebras (the only elements in the kernel\textbackslash{}nare of the form \$X\_s \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes X\_s\$) if the domain is given the Kirillov\textbackslash{}nbracket, see also [@KontsevichFormal Section 6]. This gives another\textbackslash{}nconstruction of the Lie bracket of special derivations.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: remark\textbackslash{}n*Remark 39*. Additively, the construction of Drinfeld is a special\textbackslash{}ninstance of one for cyclic operads due to Getzler--Kapranov: inspecting\textbackslash{}n[@GetzlerKapranov Definition 4.7] we note there is an equality\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{F\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{g\}\}) = \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}lambda(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{cycLie\}\},\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{g\}\})\$.\textbackslash{}nThe left side is defined for any cyclic operad \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{P\}\}\$ and\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{P\}\}\$-algebra \$A\$. If the latter is a free\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{P\}\}\$-algebra one gets an isomorphism [@GetzlerKapranov\textbackslash{}nProposition 4.9], originally outlined in Roughly, the vertical map\textbackslash{}nhas target a quotient of a Lie algebra of trees with external vertices\textbackslash{}nlabelled by \$S\$ and is determined as a map of Lie algebras by sending\textbackslash{}nthe generator \$t\_\{ij\}\$ to an edge connecting the vertices \$i\$ and \$j\$.\textbackslash{}nWe will now provide details.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe first recall the description of the Drinfeld--Kohno Lie algebra in\textbackslash{}nterms of graphs. For a finite set \$S\$, a *graph with external vertices\textbackslash{}n\$S\$* will be an unoriented finite graph \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\$ with a linear order on\textbackslash{}nits edges, a specified set \$S\$ of external vertices and possibly further\textbackslash{}ninternal vertices, satisfying\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n1.  it has no double edges,\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n2.  it has no simple loops,\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n3.  all internal vertices are at least trivalent,\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n4.  all internal vertices are connected by a path to an external vertex,\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n5.  the (open) graph obtained by deleting the external vertices is\textbackslash{}n    connected (\textbackslash{}"internally connected\textbackslash{}"),\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe let \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathsf\{CG\}\}(S)\$ [@SeveraWillwacher Section 2, 3] be the graded\textbackslash{}nvector space spanned by graph with external vertices \$S\$, modulo the\textbackslash{}nanti-symmetry relation \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}sigma = (-1)\^{}\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}sigma\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\$ where\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}sigma\$ is obtained from \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\$ by permuting the edges by\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}sigma\$, and the grading of \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\$ is\textbackslash{}n\$1-\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\# \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{edges\}+2 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\# \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{internal vertices\}\$.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nThis admits the structure of an \$L\_\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$-algebra whose differential\textbackslash{}n(increasing degree) is given by splitting each of the vertices in all\textbackslash{}npossible To see the\textbackslash{}nright square commutes, note that the vector space\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F(t)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes F(t)\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times\}\$ is spanned by\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes p(t) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}qquad \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{where \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F)\$ and \$p(t) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in F[t]\$ is irreducible\}.\$\$\textbackslash{}nThe top-right composition sends this to the element that is the image of\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha\$ in the term \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$ where \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$ is the\textbackslash{}nideal generated by \$p(t)\$. The left-bottom composition sends this to\textbackslash{}n(denoting by \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cdot\$ the multiplication in algebraic \$K\$-theory)\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}partial(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cdot p(t)) = \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cdot \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}partial(p(t)),\$\$ using the\textbackslash{}nlocalisation sequence is a sequence of \$K\_*(F)\$-modules [@Weibel V.6.1],\textbackslash{}nso that in particular \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}partial\$ is a \$K\_*(F)\$-module map. It is\textbackslash{}nstandard that in the localisation sequence \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}partial(p(t))\$ is given by\textbackslash{}n\$1\$ in the term \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$ where \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$ is the ideal\textbackslash{}ngenerated by \$p(t)\$.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nNow we use that the right vertical map is injective by the existence of\textbackslash{}ntransfer maps [@Weibel V.3.3.2] and the identification of the left and\textbackslash{}nmiddle vertical maps as those appearing in\textbackslash{}n[161](\#thm:K5)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}" reference=\textbackslash{}"thm:K5\textbackslash{}"\}, using\textbackslash{}nthat \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F)\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}xrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F(t))\}\$,\textbackslash{}nand apply the snake lemma to get an exact sequence\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{tikzcd\} 0 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_\{F(t)\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& 0 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}arrow[dll,snake left] \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}n\& H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F(t)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}textstyle \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}bigoplus\_\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\} K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F[t]/\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\})/K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& 0\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{tikzcd\}\$\$\textbackslash{}nwhich gives the results. ◻\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: remark\textbackslash{}n*Remark 165*. We can obtain slightly stronger results under the\textbackslash{}nhypothesis of the existence of a specialisation-at-zero map: the precise\textbackslash{}nclaim is that \$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{align*\}\textbackslash{}n\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}\}\_3(F(t)) \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}\}\_3(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Li\}\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}\_3(f(t)) \&\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longmapsto \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{cases\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Li\}\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathscr\{G\}\_3(f(0)) \& \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{if \$f(0) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}infty\$,\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}n0 \& \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}text\{else,\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{cases\}\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{align*\}\$\$ is well-defined. The existence of such specialisation\textbackslash{}nmaps is known on Milnor \$K\$-theory [@Weibel Theorem III.7.3] as well as\textbackslash{}nthe Bloch groups [@GoncharovEuler Section 3.2], and amounts to verifying\textbackslash{}nthat the 22-term relation is sent to zero by this map; in principle a\textbackslash{}nsufficiently determined reader could do so (possibly computer-aided). We\textbackslash{}nstrongly believe such maps exist and rather than addressing this in\textbackslash{}nad-hoc fashion here, we intend to do so in a systemic fashion in future\textbackslash{}nwork. In that case \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_5\^{}3(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_5\^{}3(F(t))\$ naturally split\textbackslash{}nby the specialisation-at-zero map.\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe obtain from this some conditions under which \$H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F))\$ is\textbackslash{}nunchanged by transcendental extensions, that is, is homotopy-invariant.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: \{\#cor:gamma-53-iso .corollary\}\textbackslash{}n**Corollary 166**. *The map \$H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F(t)))\$\textbackslash{}nis an isomorphism if one of the following conditions is satisfied:*\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n(i) *[]\{\#enum:gamma-53-iso-i label=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-i\textbackslash{}"\} \$F\$ is\textbackslash{}n    algebraically closed, or*\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n(ii) *[]\{\#enum:gamma-53-iso-ii label=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}"\}\textbackslash{}n     \$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) = 0\$ for every finite extension \$E\$ of \$F\$.*\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: proof\textbackslash{}n*Proof.* We apply the short exact sequence of\textbackslash{}n[164](\#thm:gamma-53)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"thm:gamma-53\textbackslash{}"\}. In case\textbackslash{}n[\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}[enum:gamma-53-iso-i\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}]](\#enum:gamma-53-iso-i)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"eqref\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-i\textbackslash{}"\}, since \$F\$ is algebraically closed then\textbackslash{}nall the summands of the last term are trivial. In case\textbackslash{}n[\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}[enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}]](\#enum:gamma-53-iso-ii)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"eqref\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}"\}, since \$F[t]/\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$ is a\textbackslash{}nfinite extension of \$F\$ for all \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$, each summand\textbackslash{}nvanishes. ◻\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: example\textbackslash{}n*Example 167*. Part\textbackslash{}n[\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}[enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}]](\#enum:gamma-53-iso-ii)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"eqref\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}"\} applies when \$F\$ is a number field or\textbackslash{}nhas transcendence degree \$1\$ over a finite field by\textbackslash{}n[163](\#ex:beilinson-soule-vanishing)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"ex:beilinson-soule-vanishing\textbackslash{}"\}.\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nIn fact, in some sense the converse of\textbackslash{}n[166](\#cor:gamma-53-iso)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"cor:gamma-53-iso\textbackslash{}"\}\textbackslash{}n[\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}[enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}]](\#enum:gamma-53-iso-ii)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"eqref\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}"\} is also true: Goncharov's\textbackslash{}nhomotopy-invariance conjecture in weight 3 is equivalent to the\textbackslash{}nBeilinson--Soulé vanishing conjecture in weight 2.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: corollary\textbackslash{}n**Corollary 168**. *The map \$H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F(t)))\$\textbackslash{}nis an isomorphism for every field \$F\$ if and only if\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) = 0\}\$ for every field \$E\$.*\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: proof\textbackslash{}n*Proof.* The direction \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Leftarrow\$ is a direct consequence of\textbackslash{}n[166](\#cor:gamma-53-iso)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"cor:gamma-53-iso\textbackslash{}"\}\textbackslash{}n[\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}[enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}]](\#enum:gamma-53-iso-ii)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"eqref\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"enum:gamma-53-iso-ii\textbackslash{}"\}. For the direction \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Rightarrow\$, we\textbackslash{}nuse that we have already seen that the vanishing of\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F)\}\$ is closed under pure transcendental extensions in\textbackslash{}n[163](\#ex:beilinson-soule-vanishing)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"ex:beilinson-soule-vanishing\textbackslash{}"\}. It is also true for\textbackslash{}n\$F = \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$ or \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{F\}\}\_q\$, and so it is true for all fields\textbackslash{}nif we can also show it is closed under finite extensions. It suffices to\textbackslash{}ndo so for simple extensions, and if\textbackslash{}n\$H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F(t)))\$ is an isomorphism for every\textbackslash{}nfield \$F\$ then from [164](\#thm:gamma-53)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"thm:gamma-53\textbackslash{}"\} we deduce that\textbackslash{}n\$\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F[t]/\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\})\$\$ is\textbackslash{}nsurjective for every field \$F\$ and nonzero prime ideal\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathfrak\{p\}\}\$. ◻\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe also obtain the following corollary saying that the Goncharov\textbackslash{}nconjecture in weight 3 imply the Beilinson--Soulé vanishing conjecture\textbackslash{}nin weight \$2\$.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: \{\#cor: weight 3 goncharov iff beilinson soule .corollary\}\textbackslash{}n**Corollary 169**. *The map\textbackslash{}n\$p\_F \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}colon K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F))\$ is an isomorphism for\textbackslash{}nevery field \$F\$ if and only if \$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E)=0\$ for every field \$E\$.*\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: proof\textbackslash{}n*Proof.* The direction \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Leftarrow\$ is already done in\textbackslash{}n[162](\#cor:weight-3-beilinson-soule)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"cor:weight-3-beilinson-soule\textbackslash{}"\}. For the direction\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Rightarrow\$ suppose that \$F\$ is a field such that\textbackslash{}n\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$, then\textbackslash{}n\$\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes F\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subsetneq K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes F(t)\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F(t)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes F(t)\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times.\$\$\textbackslash{}nBy [164](\#thm:gamma-53)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"thm:gamma-53\textbackslash{}"\} we know that \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_\{F(t)\})\$\textbackslash{}nand thus \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_\{F(t)\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subsetneq K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F(t)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes F(t)\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times\$\textbackslash{}nso \$m\_\{F(t)\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$ otherwise we would not have a strict inclusion.\textbackslash{}nHence \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(p\_\{F(t)\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$ and \$p\_\{F(t)\}\$ cannot be an isomorphism. ◻\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe end with a result relating the Beilinson--Soulé vanishing conjecture\textbackslash{}nin weight \$2\$ to the multiplicative structure in algebraic \$K\$-theory;\textbackslash{}nthis does not rely on our results above, but is of course related.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: \{\#prop:beilinson-soule-multiplication .proposition\}\textbackslash{}n**Proposition 170**. *If there is a field \$F\$ so that\textbackslash{}n\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$, then there exists a field \$E\$ of the same\textbackslash{}ncharacteristic such that the following product map is not injective and\textbackslash{}nnot zero\textbackslash{}n\$\$m\_E \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}colon K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes E\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(E).\$\$*\textbackslash{}n:::\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}n::: proof\textbackslash{}n*Proof.* We first prove we can find \$E\$ so that it is not injective. If\textbackslash{}n\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(F) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$ for some \$F\$ then, as algebraic \$K\$-theory\textbackslash{}ncommutes with filtered colimits, we can in fact find such an \$F\$ which\textbackslash{}nis generated by finitely many elements over \$k\$, for \$k=\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbb\{F\}\_p\$ if\textbackslash{}n\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{char\}\}(F)=p\$ and \$k=\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}\$ if \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{char\}\}(F)=0\$.\textbackslash{}nIn particular, we may assume \$F\$ has finite transcendence degree over\textbackslash{}n\$k\$.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nLet us pick \$n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{N\}\}\$ smallest so that there is a field \$E\_0\$\textbackslash{}nwith \$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E\_0) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$ and \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{trdeg\}\}\_k(E\_0)=n\$. By the\textbackslash{}nwork of Borel, \$K\_4(F)\$ vanishes for any number field \$F\$, and by the\textbackslash{}nwork of Quillen it vanishes (rationally) for any finite field too, so we\textbackslash{}nmust have \$n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ge 1\$. Let \$F\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneq k(t\_1,\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}dots,t\_n)\$ be the field\textbackslash{}nextension of \$k\$ obtained by adding \$n\$ pure transcendental variables,\textbackslash{}nso that we can view \$E\_0\$ as a finite degree field extension of \$F\_n\$.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nIn the positive characteristic \$p\$ case we factor the finite extension\textbackslash{}n\$F\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_0\$ as \$F\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_1 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_0\$ where\textbackslash{}n\$F\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_1\$ is finite and separable and \$E\_1 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_0\$ is\textbackslash{}nfinite and purely inseparable. We claim that\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E\_1)\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$ and then we can without loss of\textbackslash{}ngenerality replace \$E\_0\$ by \$E\_1\$ and assume that \$F\_n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_0\$ is\textbackslash{}nseparable. To prove the claim, if we let \$p\^{}N = [E\_0: E\_1]\$ be the\textbackslash{}ndegree then \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Frob\}\}\^{}N(E\_0) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_1\$ (as the extension is\textbackslash{}npurely inseparable) we can consider the composition\textbackslash{}n\$\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E\_0) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}xrightarrow\{\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Frob\}\}\^{}N\_*\} K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E\_1) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E\_0),\$\$\textbackslash{}nwhere the second map is induced by the inclusion \$E\_1 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset E\_0\$. This\textbackslash{}ncomposition agrees with the action of an \$N\$-fold composition of the\textbackslash{}nFrobenius, which acts by multiplication by \$p\^{}2\$ in weight 2, and hence\textbackslash{}nthe composition is multiplication by \$p\^{}\{2N\}\$, showing that the second\textbackslash{}nmap is surjective, and hence the claim.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nLet \$E\$ denote the Galois closure of \$E\_0\$ over \$F\_n\$, which is defined\textbackslash{}nby separability, then \$E\_0 \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subseteq E\$ is a finite degree extension and\textbackslash{}nhence the map induced by the inclusion\textbackslash{}n\$\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E\_0) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E)\$\$ is injective by the\textbackslash{}nexistence of transfer maps. In particular, we have\textbackslash{}n\$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$. For the rest of the proof,\textbackslash{}n\$G \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}coloneq \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathrm\{Gal\}\}(E/F\_n)\$, a finite group. We next consider the\textbackslash{}nfollowing commutative diagram\textbackslash{}n\$\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}begin\{tikzcd\}  \& K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(F\_n) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}dar\{i\_1\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar\{p\_F\}[swap]\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}simeq\} \& H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F\_n))\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}dar\{i\_2\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}[-5pt]  K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes E\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar\{m\_E\} \& K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar\{p\_E\} \& H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(E)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}rar \& 0\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}end\{tikzcd\}\$\$\textbackslash{}nwhere the bottom short exact sequence is as in\textbackslash{}n[164](\#thm:gamma-53)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"thm:gamma-53\textbackslash{}"\}, the top map is an isomorphism by\textbackslash{}n[163](\#ex:beilinson-soule-vanishing)\{reference-type=\textbackslash{}"ref+label\textbackslash{}"\textbackslash{}nreference=\textbackslash{}"ex:beilinson-soule-vanishing\textbackslash{}"\}, and the vertical maps are\textbackslash{}ninduced by the inclusion. Moreover, we claim that \$i\_2\$ is injective.\textbackslash{}nThis is trivial in positive characteristic since\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(F\_n)\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathbb\{F\}\_p)\}=0\$ by\textbackslash{}nminimality of \$n\$ and the localization sequence, so we just need to\textbackslash{}nverify the characteristic zero case. To do so, we fix an embedding\textbackslash{}n\$E \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subset \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\}\$ and observe that the Borel regulator\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\})\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}to \{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\}\$ factors over\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_5\^{}3(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\})\$ because the Borel regulators agree with\textbackslash{}nBeilinson regulators up to a nonzero constant and the latter satisfy a\textbackslash{}nproduct formula as theory of Chern classes [@Weibel V.11]. Thus the\textbackslash{}ncomposition\textbackslash{}n\$\$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\} \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_5\^{}3(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}cong\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(F\_n)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}overset\{i\_2\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(E)) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow H\^{}1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}Gamma\_3(\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\})) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}longrightarrow\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{C\}\}\$\$\textbackslash{}nwith right-most map the Borel regulator, must be injective.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nWe use this to deduce that\textbackslash{}n\$\$(K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes E\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times)\^{}G \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}subseteq \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_E).\$\$ Given\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in (K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes E\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times)\^{}G\$, since the multiplication\textbackslash{}non algebraic \$K\$-theory groups is compatible with the Galois action\textbackslash{}n(because tensor product of vector spaces is), we deduce that\textbackslash{}n\$m\_E(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(E)\^{}G\}\$. By the existence of transfer\textbackslash{}nmaps, there is a unique \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}beta \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_5\^{}\{(3)\}(F\_n)\}\$ such that\textbackslash{}n\$i\_1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}beta)=m\_E(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha)\$. Exactness of the bottom row implies that\textbackslash{}n\$p\_E(i\_1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha))=0\$ so commutativity of the diagram says that\textbackslash{}n\$i\_2(p\_F(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}beta))=0\$. Since \$i\_2\$ is injective and \$p\_F\$ is an\textbackslash{}nisomorphism, \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}beta=0\$ so \$m\_E(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha)=i\_1(\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}beta)=0\$ and thus\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}alpha \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}in \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_E)\$ as required.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nFinally, we prove that \$(K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}otimes E\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times)\^{}G \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$. Since\textbackslash{}n\$G\$ is a finite group and \$K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$, the latter contains a\textbackslash{}nfinite irreducible \$G\$-representation. Since its dual occurs in the\textbackslash{}nregular representation \$\{\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}mathds\{Q\}\}[G]\$, it suffices to prove that\textbackslash{}n\$E\^{}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}times\$ contains the regular representation; this is a consequence of\textbackslash{}n[@BDEPS Proposition 19] using that \$n \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}geq 1\$.\textbackslash{}n\textbackslash{}nTo get field \$E\$ so that the product map is not injective and not zero,\textbackslash{}ntake \$E'\$ so that \$m\_\{E'\}\$ is not injective and let \$E=E'(t)\$. By\textbackslash{}ndefinition the map \$m\_\{E'\}\$ is not injective and hence\textbackslash{}n\$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}ker(m\_\{E'\}) \textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$ and \$\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}smash\{K\_4\^{}\{(2)\}(E)\}\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}neq 0\$.   "audience": "Algebraic geometers, number theorists, K-theorists, and researchers in motivic cohomology; particularly those studying algebraic K-theory of fields, polylogarithms, and mixed Tate motives.",\\
  "key\_contributions": [\\
    "Definition and construction of the Goncharov Lie coalgebra as the E\ensuremath{\infty}-homology of general linear groups, a new bridge between algebraic K-theory and polylogarithms",\\
    "Explicit presentation of the Goncharov Lie coalgebra by generators (correlators) and four families of relations: homogeneity, cyclic symmetry, shuffle relations, and decomposition relations",\\
    "Computation of the Lie cobracket structure on the Goncharov Lie coalgebra",\\
    "Construction of motivic and Hodge realisations relating the coalgebra to mixed Tate motives and mixed Hodge structures",\\
    "Proof that K₄⁽\textsuperscript{3}⁾(F) ≅ H\textsuperscript{2}(𝒢(F))₃ and an exact sequence describing K₅⁽\textsuperscript{3}⁾(F) in terms of the polylogarithmic complex, confirming a variant of Goncharov's weight 3 conjecture",\\
    "Identification of 𝒢₁(F) with F\ensuremath{\times}, 𝒢₂(F) with the Bloch group B₂(F), and 𝒢₃(F) with the group B₃(F) of Goncharov",\\
    "Proof that the decomposition relation provides the universal functional equation for multiple polylogarithms"\\
  ],\\
  "plain\_language\_summary": "The paper develops a new algebraic structure called the Goncharov Lie coalgebra, which bridges algebraic K-theory (a classical invariant of fields measuring their arithmetic structure) and multiple polylogarithms (special functions studied for centuries in analysis and number theory). The authors construct this coalgebra using sophisticated homological methods applied to general linear groups, then present it explicitly through generators (called correlators) and relations, and compute its algebraic structure (the Lie cobracket). They establish connections to mixed Tate motives and provide motivic and Hodge realisations that link their construction to known mathematical structures. The paper's main concrete results describe K-theory groups K₄⁽\textsuperscript{3}⁾(F) and K₅⁽\textsuperscript{3}⁾(F) in symbolic terms using polylogarithmic complexes, extending classical results of Matsumoto, Milnor, Bloch, and Suslin to higher weights. These results are obtained using the Rognes rank spectral sequence, a computational tool that filters algebraic K-theory by dimension.",\\
  "tldr": "This paper introduces the Goncharov Lie coalgebra of a field, constructed from the E\ensuremath{\infty}-homology of general linear groups, and uses it to express the algebraic K-theory of fields in terms of polylogarithms."\\
\}\\
\end{quote}
